sections.intent: groove from the first beat: riff, bass, drums with side stick, shaker
the motif (call), a slide answer, the motif up a third, its answer
the lift: snare and ride, strummed archtop, the road melody
the motif on the slide guitar, then only its falling tail; metal and wood percussion; the lead answers
calm: pad, ringing arpeggios, the call slowed down; drums rebuild in the last two bars
the high point: the motif with a second voice, the full band, the call reaches G5
back to the road texture; one slide accent; a light fill into bar 1

answered.text: bass: its high-pass at 36 Hz takes 2.0 dB from the fundamental of its lowest note (E1, 41 Hz); at 21 Hz, an octave under that note, it takes 0.3 dB.
answered.reason: 36 Hz keeps the E1 fundamental within about 2 dB and keeps sub-bass out of a phone game mix, as the brief asks.

answered.text: riff: its high-pass at 70 Hz takes 2.6 dB from the fundamental of its lowest note (D2, 73 Hz); at 37 Hz, an octave under that note, it takes 0.3 dB.
answered.reason: the baritone riff leaves its lowest fundamentals to the bass on purpose (a 70 Hz high-pass).

answered.text: slide: its high-pass at 200 Hz takes 1.6 dB from the fundamental of its lowest note (B3, 247 Hz); at 123 Hz, an octave under that note, it takes 0.3 dB.
answered.reason: 200 Hz keeps the slide's low B3 within 1.6 dB; the part is a thin, high accent.

answered.text: comp: its high-pass at 90 Hz takes 1.6 dB from the fundamental of its lowest note (A2, 110 Hz); at 55 Hz, an octave under that note, it takes 0.3 dB.
answered.reason: the comp's rare low notes (A2 in the dust arpeggio) are allowed to lose some weight.

answered.text: 1 melody note on strong positions sits outside the written chord and is not resolved by step (most in slide; first E5 on Gmaj9 at bar 18 beat 4 (note slide_b018_t144_p76)). The others outside it are named in outside_chord as passing, neighbour, appoggiatura, escape, suspension, retardation, pedal or anticipation notes (Open Music Theory, Embellishing Tones). In rock, melodies leave such notes unresolved, mostly in pentatonic verses (Temperley 2007; rock-and-metal.md); elsewhere resolve each by step, change the chord under it, or write a colour tone that is meant to stay into the symbol (Cadd9, C6, Csus4).
answered.reason: the melody is pentatonic over a drone-like riff; its unresolved ninths and sixths (E over D, B over C) are the colour of the style, as in rock and blues verses.

answered.text: 11 times two parts move in parallel fifths or octaves (most between bass / riff; first octaves at bar 4 beat 4.5). Where the parts are independent voices (baroque, classical, chorale and chamber writing), two perfect consonances of the same size in a row fuse the voices and are avoided (Open Music Theory, First-Species Counterpoint): move one voice the other way or to a third or sixth. Power chords and lines doubled on purpose move in parallel; octaves inside a line doubled at the octave are left out (baroque.md).
answered.reason: the bass and the riff double the last pickup into each downbeat at the octave on purpose.

answered.text: 39 close intervals sound under their low interval limit, where voicings turn muddy (most between bass / riff; furthest under, a perfect fifth E1-B1 at bar 30 beat 4, whose limit is Bb1). Spread the voicing or move the upper note an octave up, leaving the low register to the bass. The limits are guides: soft, dark sounds bear more than loud, bright ones, and a low rumble can be meant (Hoffmann; arrangement.md, Spacing).
answered.reason: the riff is a baritone part and sits above the bass by design; the pad was moved out of the low register (three upper chord tones) after the first review.

answered.text: pad: 100% of its 40 chords are struck and released as one block. Hold a common tone over the change, move an inner voice, break the chord or vary its rhythm (development-and-groove.md; musiclib.voicing voices chords to move smoothly).
answered.reason: the pad is the delicate bed the brief asks for; its chords are held blocks under a moving band.

answered.text: Loop seam: parts leaving: metal, slide. Confirm the change of instruments at the loop point is meant.
answered.reason: the slide's last fall (bar 47) and the brake drum of bar 48 do not sound in the first second of bar 1; the riff, bass, kit, shaker and pad carry the seam.

outside_chord.source: Open Music Theory, Embellishing Tones (the kinds); Longuet-Higgins and Lee 1984 (strong positions); Temperley 2007 (rock melodies leave them unresolved)

parallels.source: Open Music Theory, First-Species Counterpoint (the rule, for independent voices); the window and the doubled share are ours

pushes.source: Tan, Lustig and Temperley 2019 (rock and pop melodies anticipate strong beats); Witek et al. 2014 (moderate syncopation)

restatement.source: Summach 2011 (pop sections state and restate an idea); Caplin 1998 (the sentence); the 8 bars are ours

widespread_lowpass.source: Senior 2012 (Sound On Sound, Q&A): widespread low-pass filtering seldom helps a mix and easily dulls it; the 12 kHz (the lower edge of air in the mixing books listed by Moffat, De Man and Reiss 2022), the half and the three parts are ours

tempo_range.source: the tempo ranges the entries' sources give (their maps' tempo cells, `tempo_bpm`); reading half and double time as inside is ours

plan.identity: a baritone riff on an open E that rises into beat 2 and leaves the bar's second half to the drums; a five-note call (B D | E . D B ... E) that starts in that space and slides into its high note; G-major pitch classes only

high_point.means: the call with a second voice, the full kit with snare and crash, strums, and the call's high variant reaching G5

sections.what_differs: the loop's first bar: groove at once, no melody
the call enters in the riff's space; ghost hats; a slide answer
C G D Em: the relative-major lift, a chord every bar, snare and ride, strums, the road melody
the motif moves to the slide guitar; brake drum, guiro, anvil; side stick again
no riff for six bars, pad and ringing arpeggios, the call in long notes; the drums rebuild in its last two bars
the motif with a second voice, snare backbeat, crash, strums
the ignition texture again, one slide accent, a light fill into bar 1
